quick: Apply a thin film to affected skin twice daily (gel 15% / cream 20% / foam 15%)
Considered low risk; use only if clearly needed
Minimal systemic absorption; apply away from breast
No interaction; alcohol-based products may sting
summary: Azelaic acid is a topical dicarboxylic acid used for inflammatory papulopustular rosacea (15% gel/foam) and mild-to-moderate acne vulgaris (20% cream). It has antimicrobial, anticomedonal and antikeratinising actions with negligible systemic absorption. Applied twice daily to clean dry skin; common effects are local burning, stinging and itching, and rarely hypopigmentation, especially in darker skin.
indications: Topical treatment of inflammatory papules and pustules of mild to moderate rosacea (15% gel/foam)
Topical treatment of mild to moderate acne vulgaris (20% cream)

dosage.d: Apply a thin layer to the affected facial skin twice daily (morning and evening)
dosage.n: Use after gently cleansing and drying skin

dosage.d: Apply a thin film and gently massage into affected areas twice daily
dosage.n: Reassess if no improvement after ~4 weeks; benefit may take weeks

dosage.d: 20% cream as for adults in acne; safety in younger children not established
dosage.n: Rosacea products not established in children

admin: Wash and dry skin gently before applying; avoid harsh/abrasive or alcoholic cleansers
Apply a thin film to affected areas only and wash hands after use (foam is flammable - avoid fire/flame/smoking during and right after application)
Avoid contact with eyes, mouth and other mucous membranes; rinse with water if contact occurs
Cosmetics may be applied after the product has dried
moa: Azelaic acid has antimicrobial activity against Cutibacterium acnes and a direct anti-inflammatory/antioxidant effect (scavenging reactive oxygen species and reducing neutrophil-derived radicals). In acne it also normalises disturbed follicular keratinisation (anticomedonal). Its action in rosacea is not fully defined.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to azelaic acid or any formulation component (e.g. propylene glycol)
relative: Application to broken or eczematous skin (increased irritation)

preg: Systemic absorption is negligible. Animal data and limited human use suggest low risk; use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: Negligible systemic absorption; small amounts in milk are expected to be clinically insignificant. If applied to the chest, do so after feeding and ensure the infant does not contact treated skin.
renal: No dose adjustment needed - systemic absorption after topical use is negligible.
hepatic: No dose adjustment needed - systemic absorption after topical use is negligible.

minor: Other topical irritants/peeling agents (benzoyl peroxide, retinoids, alpha-hydroxy acids) - may add to local irritation if used together
interactions.alcohol: No systemic interaction; alcohol-containing skin products may increase stinging.

common: Burning, stinging or tingling at the application site
rare: Hypopigmentation (especially in patients with darker skin)

monitoring: Skin pigmentation, particularly in patients with darker complexions
Improvement in lesions over weeks of therapy
Asthma symptoms in known asthmatics (rare reports of worsening)
counsel: Apply a thin layer to clean, dry skin twice a day and wash your hands afterwards
Mild burning, stinging or itching is common at first and usually settles
Improvement can take several weeks - keep using it as directed
Avoid getting it in your eyes, mouth or nose; rinse with water if it happens
Tell your doctor if you notice lightening of the skin or your asthma worsens; the foam is flammable so keep away from flame while applying
pk: Negligible systemic peak after topical application
~12 hours for the small absorbed fraction
Store at controlled room temperature; do not freeze; foam is flammable
pearls: Negligible systemic absorption - safe across renal/hepatic impairment with no monitoring of bloods
15% gel/foam for rosacea; 20% cream for acne - match the formulation to the indication
Can cause hypopigmentation, especially in darker skin - monitor for colour change
Local burning/stinging is common early and usually transient
Foam formulation is flammable - avoid fire, flame and smoking during application
missed: If you miss an application, apply it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next application, skip the missed one and continue your usual twice-daily routine - do not apply extra to catch up.
overdose: Topical overdose or accidental ingestion is expected to cause only local irritation given negligible systemic absorption. Excessive application may increase skin irritation; manage by reducing frequency and giving symptomatic skin care.
